quotes.text: We don't hear enough artist's out there now who focus on tone over image. She never let her personal life represent her music and for that I admire and adore her.

I think it's testimony to her greatness that she could fit in all kinds of settings, from very formal orchestras to something as loose and intimate as Count Basie's organ. She worked in a wide variety of settings and sounded great in virtually all of them.
Great art like Garland's is above such considerations. She defines her own categories as she goes along.

Like Billie Holiday and Frank Sinatra, she's such a commanding performer that when she starts singing you have to stop what you're doing and give her your full attention. It's not even like you have any choice in the matter!

She delivers it with such amazing conviction that it positively makes my hair stand on end. She sings it like a combination of national anthem and spiritual. It seems patriotic and religious. And yet, between Garland and Cole Porter, there's an awful lot of self-deflating wit in there as well. She touches a dozens different places in the heart at once.
